avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and pays an organization to green private and institutional land. Boroughs add their own means: money from the parks fund, equipment rental, blue-collar worker teams. Exemptions also allow tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and to Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its reserved parks fund toward buying trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expansion at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with renovating the parc Pratt chalet and redeveloping its surroundings, including plant installation, partly funded by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome district, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees intended for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.
deneigement.enBref: The City and boroughs rent machinery with operators for snow clearing, snow loading and spring cleanup, and hire companies to clear snow from public squares and parking lots. Several turnkey snow removal and towing contracts are being extended or awarded for upcoming seasons. Some boroughs are also amending their by-laws covering contractors who clear snow from private land.

etapes.texte: Boroughs are renting sweeper trucks, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper with operators to remove abrasives and clean streets, sidewalks and bike paths. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an expense of $574,920.99, taxes included, for the rental of sweepers and tanker trucks [CA26 27 0008].

etapes.titre: Snow removal from downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie hires companies for the maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal of Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises and six public squares, including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending by one year the snow removal services for the Quartier des Spectacles, which includes spreading abrasives and snow loading [CA26 24 0067].

Montréal-Nord pays for an additional grader rental, and Saint-Léonard draws $200,000 from its surpluses for staff pay and the purchase of abrasives [CA26 13 0121]. Verdun offers to city council to provide its own staff for the snow disposal site during loading operations.

The City is extending by twelve months turnkey snow removal contracts in Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro, towing contracts, and equipment rentals with operators in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. Ville-Marie and Anjou are also extending rentals of loader tractors and a grader, and the snow removal of the Jacinthe-Fyfe building parking lot is renewed.

etapes.titre: New snow removal and towing contracts
etapes.texte: City council awards turnkey snow removal contracts for four winter seasons in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Sud-Ouest, following the report from the Commission sur l'examen des contrats. It also awards towing services related to snow removal in Montréal-Nord for three winter seasons.

aSurveiller.texte: Saint-Léonard indicates that the adoption of its by-law on permits for snow removal contractors is planned for September 8, 2026, with a notice of coming into force on September 9, 2026.
The extended snow removal equipment rental services in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie begin on November 1, 2026 and continue until March 31, 2027.
The extended towing contracts begin on November 15, 2026.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and launching work on its water networks: rehabilitation of pipes in several boroughs, reconstruction of pipes and streets, and replacement of lead water service connections. It is also continuing work at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, including construction of the oxygen production unit linked to the ozone disinfection project. It is adopting loan by-laws to pay for these projects.

etapes.texte: The City is awarding contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes by lining them and to redo roadways, on streets in the West Island, downtown and the east end of the island. These contracts also include replacing lead water service connections, on both the public and private sides.

aSurveiller.texte: Commissioning of the ozone plant expected in 2029, with contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 due to be completed in the last quarter of 2028.
Rehabilitation work on a 600 mm pipe along the autoroute 15 Nord: starting in September 2026, ending no later than December 18, 2026.
Shutdown of incinerator 2 starting the first week of October 2026 and of incinerator 4 in January 2027, about six weeks each.
Work on rue de la Cathédrale extended by 77 days: the end date moves from December 2026 to March 2027.
Leak detection on main pipes: work from July 2026 to June 2028.

frederic-back.titre: Frédéric-Back Park and Saint-Michel Environmental Complex
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system modernization.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on three fronts at Frédéric-Back park and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel: a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, the modernization of electrical facilities linked to biogas capture, and park maintenance. It is also asking Québec for financial aid for an east-west pedestrian and bike link with a footbridge. At the same time, the borough is redeveloping rue De Louvain, along the edge of the park.

etapes.titre: Funding request for the east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for funding of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre trail crossing the park from east to west, including a footbridge about 150 metres long (CG26 0121). The project also includes rainwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The agglomeration approves the construction of a research, training and community production greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then delegates the project to city council (CG26 0124). The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to carry it out and city council accepts (CA26 14 0039, CM26 0363).

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract worth $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, which includes a new 25 kV power supply, a backup generator and an automated system to manage biogas capture (CG26 0223). It also assigns two companies general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months (CG26 0224).

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between Frédéric-Back park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers and water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

The City is extending by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, for $296,349.21 more, taxes included. The compost, made from leaves collected in parks and streets, is used in particular for the development of Frédéric-Back park (CG26 0320).

The borough awards Les industries Harnois inc. the supply and installation of the greenhouse complex, for a maximum amount of $499,865.92, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $574,845.80. The project involves two greenhouses with structure, envelope, natural ventilation, soil, interior divisions and condensation water management.

aSurveiller.texte: Greenhouses: delivery of the infrastructure in July 2026, work starting in August 2026 and expected completion in December 2026, according to the borough's file.
Greenhouses expected to come into service in winter 2027.
The call for projects under the ministère des Transports' funding program, for the footbridge and the east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Rue De Louvain: work in three phases, from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
Park maintenance: contracts from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028; 26 hectares will be added to the park in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.
Rental of the screener and loader tractor from June 20 to October 15, 2026.

grand-parc-ouest.description: The largest municipal park in Canada, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the stone walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract with Les Constructions H2D inc. to rebuild heritage walls along chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones, surplus mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase; the work, 60% complete as of December 1, 2025, resumes on May 15, 2026.

etapes.titre: Application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques night sky
etapes.texte: The City is filing the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, described as covering 330 hectares, for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The filing involves no expense; the City commits to producing a lighting management plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping the site accessible in the evening.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The City is listing the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération, along with conservation plans. It is also taking note of the 2025 area summary.

The City is awarding Gendron Gestion Civil inc. the contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub, for a total expense of $481,850.45. The work includes the new culvert, roadway resurfacing, and replacement of guardrails.

aSurveiller.texte: Expected completion of work on the chemin de Senneville stone walls: July 10, 2026.
Filing of the Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan: February 2027.
Response from DarkSky International on the designation: April 2027.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to open warming centres, and funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It is also extending a Ville-Marie public works team dedicated to cleanliness related to homelessness to other boroughs. Finally, it is setting up a framework for accepting private donations for shelter and housing.

etapes.texte: The City lends, free of charge, the former Sainte-Bibiane church to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former Recluses Missionnaires monastery to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the former Bain St-Denis to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN, for the winter of 2025-2026. The loan of the Bain St-Denis covers 15,406 square feet, from February 1 to April 30, 2026, for about 20 people [CG26 0116].

etapes.titre: Warming centres and outreach workers funded by boroughs
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville extends COHAB inc.'s contract to operate a warming centre during the winter of 2025-2026. Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026 [CA26 210012].

The City grants $5,407,736 to 15 organizations for new homelessness-related projects and adds $3,942,461 to 10 already-funded organizations, over three years, until December 31, 2028, under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs. The projects cover inclusion, coexistence in public space, and awareness-raising.

etapes.titre: Nuit des sans-abri and support on rue Notre-Dame
etapes.texte: The City pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. It also grants $149,520 to the Mission Old Brewery to help people from the encampment area on rue Notre-Dame, in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, move toward shelter and housing.

aSurveiller.texte: The Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Financial support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: City council amended two leases for land south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent: a 2,787-square-metre lot leased to the Société de transport de Montréal for $49,293 in total, and an 836-square-metre lot leased to a paid parking company for $45,049 before taxes.

The City is extending, free of charge, the loan of a 10,000-square-foot lot to an organization that grows a vegetable garden there, and of a 3,316-square-metre lot to an urban agriculture organization for sunflowers and a greenhouse. City council also agreed to prepare itself a free lease of 78,244 square feet, at the southeast corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade, for programming activities.

etapes.titre: Contract to redevelop rue de Louvain
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension awarded a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 including taxes, and authorized total spending of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The central street gets a name
etapes.texte: City council named the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name came from a public call for suggestions held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Programming and events on the site
etapes.texte: The borough granted $35,000 to an organization to design and carry out the Esplanade-Louvain pop-up space, at 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, from June 9 to December 31, 2026. It also authorized, on a vacant lot at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, an event-based and temporary use: multimedia activity, shows, street food, a drink service and recreational activities.

etapes.titre: New street, networks and remediated soil
etapes.texte: The City awarded a company a contract worth $10,311,940.25 including taxes to build a street with sewer, water main, roadway, lighting and soil management in the eco-district, for total spending of $15,366,336, and added $2,007,312.15 net to remediate the soil of the former gas station area. The borough also adopted a second draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest and the construction of a group of buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: Work on rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel is happening in three phases: from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
The loan of the land for the sunflowers and the greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026, to October 31, 2027.
The lease for programming activities covers two periods from April 1 to October 31, in 2026 and in 2027.
Four other public spaces on the site remain to be named by the end of development, expected around 2032.
The parking lease with the Société de transport de Montréal starts on October 1, 2026, for three years and a maximum of 92 days per year.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanization and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is adjusting collection days and frequency in several boroughs, buying bins and extending food waste treatment contracts while waiting for the Montréal-Est biomethanization centre to come into service. It is also awarding services related to ecocentres and former disposal sites. The 2025 residual materials management report and the accountability report for the 2020-2025 master plan were tabled at the urban agglomeration council.

etapes.texte: The City is extending Recyclage Notre-Dame inc.'s contracts for composting or biomethanization of food waste from the east of the agglomeration by six months, then by another six months, until February 28, 2027. The materials are transferred in Montréal-Est, then composted in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and in Moose Creek, Ontario, because the start-up of the Montréal-Est centre is not confirmed.

Several boroughs are awarding hydro-excavation contracts including residual materials treatment, following public call for tenders 25-21256. These services are used to dig using pressurized water near water and sewer pipes, until December 31, 2028.

The City is extending Waste Connections of Canada inc. / Enviro Connexions contracts for 12 months for the collection and disposal of waste from front-loading and semi-underground containers, kept in place until October 31, 2027. It is also extending until October 31, 2027 the supply and transport of containers for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre, a contract transferred to GFL Environmental inc.

Recyc-Matelas inc. is awarded the contract for the collection, transport and recovery of mattresses and box springs from the agglomeration's ecocentres, for $734,690.25 including taxes over 28 months. The City is also retaining Consultants AECOM inc. and Terrapex Environnement ltée for studies related to construction on former disposal sites, and is extending the discharge authorization management software from Diffusion Solutions Intégrées inc.

aSurveiller.texte: Recyclage Notre-Dame inc.'s food waste treatment contracts run until February 28, 2027; the City can terminate them with 30 days' notice if the Montréal-Est centre becomes fully operational.

Collection schedules change on November 1, 2026 in Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, where the spacing of garbage collection is being done in two phases, in fall 2026 and fall 2027.
The loan of dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until the contribution is used up, and no later than December 31, 2026.
Garbage collection by containers and the supply of containers at the Saint-Laurent ecocentre are provided until October 31, 2027.
The discharge authorization management software is extended from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, water supply for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the development of the former racetrack site, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It obtained from the Québec government an additional delay to sell a first piece of land, adopted loan by-laws for the site improvements and water supply system, and guaranteed a loan used to pay for studies. At the same time, it is leasing land on the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: Deadline postponed to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The postponement does not involve any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed remain the same.

The City adopts a $29,000,000 loan for soil remediation, sewers, the water supply system, street redevelopment, and land purchases for the urban project. It also adopts a $12,000,000 loan to build water supply trunk mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella.

etapes.titre: Four buildings authorized on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough adopts a draft resolution authorizing four residential buildings in four phases at 7301, boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160, rue Namur, one of which will house a municipal sports and recreation centre. The developer will pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and facilities; a public consultation meeting will be held.

aSurveiller.texte: October 31, 2027: deadline given to the City to sell a first piece of land on the site.
April 30, 2028: end of the transition nursery's lease, which began May 1, 2026.
March 31, 2028: end of the extended lease of the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora.
2031: deadline set by Ottawa for completing the subsidized infrastructure.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: This year, the City is funding the design and redevelopment work of parks in several boroughs, from parc Le Prévost to parc Percy-Walters, often including play areas, water play features and plantings. Several projects come from Montréal's participatory budget. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, the City is repairing structures, submitting an application for an international designation and listing an area in the registry of protected natural habitats.

etapes.titre: Studies and design of new developments
etapes.texte: The City awards the winning team of an architecture competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included [CM26 0082]. It also provides funding to Verdun for soil studies at parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard and launches a public art competition for the parc des Eaux-Cachées.

etapes.titre: Parc d'Argenson and parc sportif du Sud-Ouest
etapes.texte: Le Sud-Ouest signs an agreement with Hydro-Québec to obtain $154,000 and carry out phase 4 of parc d'Argenson [CA26 22 0016]. The City awards a contract to St-Denis Thompson inc. to develop a sports park between rues Saint-Patrick, Hadley, Roberval and Cabot.

The City adds funds to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville and awards a contract to rebuild a culvert under the same road, at the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche. It submits the application for the secteur du Cap-Saint-Jacques for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and lists the secteur de l'Anse-à-l'Orme in the registry of protected natural habitats.

The City and the boroughs adjust contracts already awarded: supervision of work at parc du Bassin-à-Bois, budget transfers for parcs des Hirondelles and du Sault-au-Récollet, and an additional amount to the architects of parc Denise-Morelle.

City council removes a 810.2 m² section of street from the public domain to add it to parc Campbell Ouest [CM26 0704]. The City pays $168,472.14 to Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension for the environmental remediation of parc George-Vernot and its supervision.

aSurveiller.texte: Parc des Eaux-Cachées: selection of the winning public art project in October 2026, contract in December 2026, installation of the artwork in 2028.
Parc Denise-Morelle: work from early August 2026 to November 2026.
Parc Percy-Walters: work from July to November 2026, with a continuation in spring 2027.
Parc J.O.R.-Leduc: work from August 2026 to June 2028.
Parc du Bassin-à-Bois: final acceptance of the work in June 2027.
Cap-Saint-Jacques: lighting plan submitted in February 2027, DarkSky response in April 2027, site compliance in April 2032.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and commercial animation ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is closing streets to traffic for the summer and funding commercial development corporations that animate them. Boroughs are adopting the ordinances that govern these pedestrian streets: hours, noise, terraces, and the sale of food and drinks. The City is also acting on public squares: development, naming, change of use of a piece of land.

etapes.titre: Subsidy rules and end of a lawsuit
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law allowing it to subsidize its commercial development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre of pedestrianized street, with applications to be submitted by no later than February 16, 2026. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer.

The executive committee transfers $2,694,500 to six boroughs for pedestrian streets on commercial arteries, with each project required to close the street for at least eight consecutive weeks. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN on a ramp of chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges from April 1 to October 31, 2026, and Ville-Marie bans traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations.

Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension pays $102,045 to the Société de développement commercial du Quartier Villeray to pedestrianize rue Villeray, between rue Lajeunesse and avenue De Gaspé. Ville-Marie grants $375,500 to the Société de développement commercial du Village for rue Sainte-Catherine Est, and Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard.

Outremont closes avenue Bernard between avenue Bloomfield and the lane east of avenue Wiseman from May 19 to September 24, 2026. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce turns avenue Royal and avenue Madison into public squares from June 1 to October 31, 2026, while Ville-Marie changes the dates of three of its pedestrianizations.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal closes avenue du Mont-Royal and avenue Duluth and awards a $287,724.94 contract to the organization SOCIOCYCLE to transport, on request, people with reduced mobility and seniors on the pedestrian street. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve closes rue Ontario Est between rue Darling and boulevard Pie-IX and removes paid parking spaces, and Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce supports the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal bans amplified instruments on its pedestrian streets and music between 9 p.m. and 8 a.m., while Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce authorizes a commercial promotion on a closed street on avenue de Monkland and the City pays $40,000 to animate the pedestrian street Notre-Dame Ouest. City council names "place Chez-Marguerite" a public square in Montréal-Nord and changes the use of an 899 square metre piece of land at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier, which becomes a local park.

aSurveiller.texte: Rue Ontario Est remains closed to cars until September 18, 2026; parking meters return on September 17, 2026.
Avenue Lacombe is closed to cars from September 10 to 13, 2026.
Avenue Bernard fully reopens to traffic on September 25, 2026.
Boroughs funded by the executive committee report back in November 2026 and return unspent money in December 2026.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws that each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie reviews its urban planning, special project and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, after public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough lengthens its list of heritage-interest buildings, regulates housing and service establishments for people experiencing residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects and site planning and architectural integration plans. A public meeting was held on March 18, 2026 and a written consultation took place from March 11 to 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and building footprint ratio in the sector bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requests six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. After the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the City revised the view corridor and height plans; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and makes certain work subject to approval in the declared heritage site of Mont-Royal.

Saint-Léonard takes note of two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on the demolition of buildings, after a public consultation meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève states it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027 as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other blocks are announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests an extension until June 16, 2027 to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The City of Montréal's Police Department (Service de police de la Ville de Montréal): contracts, neighbourhood police stations, council motions.
securite-publique.enBref: This year, the City is funding and purchasing equipment for its police department: motorcycles, vans, a patrol boat, and practice ammunition. It is also renewing leases for neighbourhood police stations and premises, extending building services contracts, and lending police officers to the Royal Canadian Mounted Police and to the Sûreté du Québec. Borough councils have adopted motions in support of the Police Department.

etapes.titre: Loan and purchase of police equipment
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a loan by-law of $10,880,000 to purchase and replace public safety-related equipment between 2026 and 2030 (CG26 0073). The City then purchases motorcycles, two 4 x 4 vans, a harbour patrol boat with its trailer, and enters into an agreement for 9 mm calibre practice ammunition.

The City awards a contract of $935,681.50, taxes included, to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building, at 1515 chemin Remembrance (CG26 0163). It also entrusts a group of firms with the plans, specifications and supervision of work for the permanent 9-1-1 relief centre.

etapes.titre: Leases for neighbourhood police stations and premises
etapes.texte: The City leases 50 parking spaces at 260 boulevard De Maisonneuve for headquarters vehicles, and extends the lease of the training centre on rue Ernest-Cormier, in Anjou. It also renews the leases for neighbourhood police station 15, in Verdun, neighbourhood police station 26, on avenue Mountain Sights, and the subway unit premises of neighbourhood police station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est.

aSurveiller.texte: Fundraising day for the Fraternité des policiers et policières at neighbourhood police station 46, for which the Anjou borough purchased tickets.
Start of the ten-year lease for the subway unit premises of neighbourhood police station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, on February 1, 2027.
Delivery of the harbour patrol boat and its trailer no later than March 1, 2027.
Completion of the work to replace the oil heating system of the cavalry building on September 30, 2027.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides about the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the budget and borrowings of the Société de transport de Montréal, sells or leases it land for its facilities, and oversees construction work related to the metro and the REM. It also entrusts the STM with municipal work near future stations on the blue line and gives it financial support for a sporting event.

etapes.texte: City council and the urban agglomeration council approve the STM's 2026 budget and 2026-2035 capital program, a balanced budget of $1,804,314,410 (CG26 0022). They also sign a 36-month agreement with Produits Suncor Énergie to supply clear diesel and diesel containing renewable fuel, for a maximum of $41,944,604.63 taxes included, plus contingencies.

The City leases to the STM a 2,787 square metre plot of land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, south of rue de Louvain, for parking its agents' vehicles, for a total rent of $49,293. The Ahuntsic-Cartierville borough establishes and removes bus waiting posts in its territory, as part of the overhaul of the bus network.

The City signs an agreement with the STM to build a pavilion at parc Irma-LeVasseur, attached to the metro ventilation station on avenue Wiseman, in Outremont. It then entrusts the STM with carrying out its own work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, and will pay it up to $3,808,451.29 taxes included.

etapes.titre: Advertising, public access and construction work
etapes.texte: The City purchases advertising space from Astral Affichage in the metro and buses for Espace pour la vie, for a maximum of $172,462.50 taxes included. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce signs an agreement with the STM for access to a vacant lot on boulevard Décarie, Ville-Marie authorizes day and night work in the green line tunnel, and the City does not object to the reconstruction of a bridge-tunnel above the REM.

The City sells to the STM a 364.3 square metre plot of land at place Saint-Henri, for $495,150 plus taxes, to expand the Place-Saint-Henri station entrance. It also sells it land in Verdun, for $257,425 plus taxes, for the Rielle ventilation station, and commits to selling it a portion of rue Jean-Brillant, for $115,000 plus taxes, where the STM will build a rectifier station.

etapes.titre: Sporting event and motion on the tunnel boring machine
etapes.texte: The City grants $382,000 to the STM to strengthen bus and metro service during the 2026 UCI Road World Championships, and $120,000 to the Société du parc Jean-Drapeau. City council adopts a motion asking the Québec government to study the conditions for keeping the tunnel boring machine "Lisette" in Montréal after the blue line extension.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the land on rue de Louvain begins on October 1, 2026 and lasts three years, at 92 days per year.
Contracts for the work at Pie-IX and Viau stations must be awarded in August and October 2026; the City's work is integrated in 2028-2029 and the blue line stations are expected to open in 2031.
Work on the Rielle ventilation station, in Verdun, must continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer holidays, for the reconstruction of the bridge-tunnel; the work is expected to continue until March 2028.
Authorization from the ministère des Affaires municipales for borrowings related to the MR-73 and the repair of surface buildings is expected in November 2026.

velo.titre: Bikeways: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the public bike-share system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City is buying bikes, docking points and station parts for the BIXI system, and having new stations installed as part of street construction projects. It is also funding the repair of existing bike paths, including the REV Lajeunesse, and regularizing rents for Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs, for their part, oversee the development and maintenance of their own bike paths.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes spending of $100,000, taxes included, for concrete, de-icing salt and abrasives intended in part for bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville awards Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. the rental of a mini sweeper with operator for spring cleaning of paths less than 1.8 metres wide, for $153,395.05, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Sustainable mobility corridors in the east
etapes.texte: City council adds $3,400,000, taxes included, to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for traffic lights, civil and electrical work and bike paths in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, on rue Hochelaga and rue du Havre. The contract reaches $11,399,999.99, taxes included.

City council approves a $125,167.62 agreement, taxes included, with Hydro-Québec for rents from 2014 to 2025 on 19 pieces of land used for bike paths, parks and community gardens. It then approves a 10-year lease, with total rent of $46,896, taxes included, to rent about 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for bike path purposes.

etapes.titre: Repair of the REV Lajeunesse and rue Lajoie
etapes.texte: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to take charge of repairing sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepts this offer as well as Ville-Marie's offer for roadway and bike path work under the Plan Vélo 2019. Outremont files a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path.

aSurveiller.texte: For the REV Lajeunesse, the file indicates a call for tenders in May 2026, the awarding of contracts in June, and work from July to August 2026.
The UCI Road World Championships are held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; stretches along the route are targeted by the roadway work in Ville-Marie.
The repair of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between the west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is listed at $570,000 in 2027.
Work on the sustainable mobility corridors resumes in spring 2026, for completion in spring or summer 2026.
